title: Introduction
desc: This is a cultivation world where many cultivators compete and conflicts rage on all sides.

title: Realm
desc: The world's underlying standard realms, from weak to strong, are Qi Refinement, Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, and Nascent Soul. Each realm has Early, Middle, and Late stages. Different traditions may use aliases, but rules are calculated by this standard sequence.

title: Lifespan
desc: Every character has a lifespan limit. When lifespan is exhausted, death follows; realm breakthroughs usually extend lifespan, while failed breakthroughs may shorten it.

title: Death
desc: HP dropping below 0 also causes death.

title: Region
desc: Different regions have different effects; doing the right thing in the right region yields twice the result with half the effort.

title: Cultivation
desc: Cultivation accumulates power until the current rank reaches its bottleneck. Breakthroughs can succeed or fail; success advances the character to the next rank, while failure may carry a cost.

title: Spirit Root
desc: Spirit roots are composed of five elements (Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth), divided into Single, Dual, and Heavenly Spirit Roots. Five elements interaction: Metal overcomes Wood, Wood overcomes Earth, Earth overcomes Water, Water overcomes Fire, Fire overcomes Metal. Heavenly Spirit Root contains all five elements and has an extra bonus during breakthrough. Cultivation efficiency is highest in regions matching one's own spirit root attribute.

title: World Qi
desc: The world undergoes celestial changes (such as Qi Tides) every few years, affecting character abilities.

title: Spirit Stone
desc: The common currency of the cultivation world. Can be used to buy artifacts and elixirs, obtained through gathering, trading, or plundering.

title: Sect
desc: A shelter for cultivators. Joining a sect allows learning unique techniques and gaining protection from fellow disciples; rogue cultivators are free but lack resources.

title: Battle
desc: Survival of the fittest; realm suppression is huge, high-realm cultivators have an absolute advantage over low-realm ones. If the opponent dies, the winner can plunder the loser's belongings.

title: Action
desc: You have a series of executable actions. Pay attention to the effects, restrictions, regions, and time of actions.

title: Equipment & Elixir
desc: Weapons, auxiliary equipment, and elixirs provide extra bonuses. High-grade equipment and suitable elixirs can greatly improve a cultivator's survival and combat ability.

title: Shopping
desc: In city regions, you can buy Qi Refinement-grade elixirs and weapons. Purchased elixirs are consumed immediately to strengthen the character; purchased weapons can switch the character to a more suitable weapon type.

title: Auction
desc: Every uncertain period of time, there will be an auction organized by a mysterious person, perhaps selling good goods.

title: Secret Realm
desc: Secret realms open every few years. Entering a secret realm may encounter danger, but may also obtain high-level artifacts and techniques.

title: Orthodoxy
desc: Different orthodoxies have different cultivation methods. Taoists respire, Martial Artists practice Body Tempering, Buddhists meditate, and Confucians educate the people.

title: Ranking
desc: The cultivation world features the Heaven, Earth, and Human Rankings, as well as the Sect Ranking. The three personal rankings are grouped by equivalent standard realm: Heaven records Nascent Soul-tier experts, Earth records Core Formation-tier experts, and Human records Foundation Establishment-tier experts. The Sect Ranking ranks sects by total power.

title: Dynasty
desc: Mortal dynasties rule the realm, maintaining worldly order and borders. Emperors live no longer than ordinary mortals, and when one dies, a new emperor succeeds to the throne.

title: Official Rank
desc: Cultivators may govern for the imperial court, building court reputation and receiving salary. With enough reputation they can be promoted; the higher the office, the greater the salary and luck. If they neglect governance for too long, their reputation will gradually decline.

title: Race
desc: The world contains both human and yao cultivators. Yao include fox, wolf, bird, snake, turtle, and other races, each with different instincts: foxes are clever and sly, wolves are fierce hunters, birds excel at migration and scouting, snakes are patient and venomous, and turtles are long-lived and defensive. Yao can cultivate and join sects that accept them, but some sects that emphasize human rites or Confucian order do not accept yao.

title: Realm Aliases
desc: The same cultivation ranks have different names in each tradition: Daoists and rogue cultivators use Qi Refinement, Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, and Nascent Soul; martial cultivators use Body Tempering, Tendon-Tempering, Martial Master, and Martial Saint; Confucian cultivators use Vital Qi Cultivation, Principle Illumination, Mandate Establishment, and Great Scholar; Buddhist cultivators use Novice Monk, Monk, Arhat, and Bodhisattva; yao cultivators use Spirit Awakening, Form Transformation, Demon Core, and Demon King. These names map to the same underlying realm sequence; they change narrative and interface wording, but not breakthrough, power, lifespan, item grade, or other rules.

title: Gu
desc: Gu arts require a cultivator to carry a Gu tool and have the ability to inflict Gu before applying it to an observable target. Different Gu act in different ways: Mind-Sinking Gu subtly shifts relationships, Blood-Devouring Gu periodically damages life, while Essence-Eroding Gu and Heart-Disordering Gu disturb cultivation. Inflicting Gu has a success rate affected by the tool, the caster's bonuses, and the target's Gu resistance; failure may be detected and harm the relationship.

title: Formations
desc: Formations require a cultivator to carry a formation disk and have formation-setting ability before placing a temporary regional effect at the current location. Different formations suit different regions: cultivation grounds and sect regions can hold spirit-gathering, mountain-guarding, clarity, and similar arrays; cities can hold healing arrays; mines, herb fields, and beast domains can hold vein-seeking, wood-growth, and beast-driving arrays. Formations consume spirit stones and expire after their duration ends.

title: Opportunity
desc: Cultivators may occasionally feel a sudden stir of fate, sensing that a person or place is tied to their own opportunity. If they follow the sense, they may gain treasure or a boon, return empty-handed, or meet danger; if they delay too long, the opportunity fades away.
